newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Former Jamaica Prime Minister Manley dead at 72.
newsitem.headline: Former Jamaica Prime Minister Manley dead at 72.

text.p: Michael Manley, a former Prime Minister of Jamaica and a legendary figure in Caribbean politics, has died after a long battle with prostate cancer, his family said on Friday. He was 72.
Manley died "peacefully" at 11:45 Thursday night at his home in Kingston, according to a statement issued by his family.
Manley was prime minister of Jamaica from 1972 until 1980 and again from 1989 to 1992.

He was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 1990 and went through a severe bout of pneumonia at the same time. The illnesses eventually forced him to resign from office before his term was over. His health had been in decline since.

He was a leader in numerous third world causes, including liberation efforts in Africa. He was a longtime ally of Cuban President Fidel Castro and champion of a new global economic order and better commodity prices for developing nations.
Manley was one of the signers of the original treaty that created the Caribbean Community and was a leader in efforts to integrate the far-flung islands of the region.
